title: Access lifecycle correlator: enforce SSO/SCIM policies, scheduled reviews, and tamper-evident evidence exports
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers require a single, auditable enforcement plane that correlates identity events (SSO/SAML assertions, SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning, and RBAC role changes) with residency and retention policies so periodic access reviews are meaningful and evidence exports are tamper-evident. Current gaps: (1) SCIM deprovision events can be delayed and not tied to policy reason codes; (2) SSO session exceptions exist for cross-tenant administration; (3) periodic review artifacts are assembled manually from multiple logs; (4) evidence exports lack an immutable signing step required by some auditors.

Goal: Build the "Access Lifecycle Correlator" service and orchestration that: (a) enforces conditional SSO and session policies based on tenant residency and privileged role; (b) improves SCIM reconciliation to surface provisioning drift and attach policy reason codes; (c) automates scheduled access review runs with pre-built reviewer packs and reviewer assignments; (d) generates tamper-evident, signed evidence bundles (JSONL + manifest + signature) and pushes them to the customer's evidence storage or SIEM endpoint.

Scope: backend enforcement, the SCIM reconciliation pipeline, a small Console UI for scheduling and reviewer handoff, audit export format, and integrations for KMS signing. Excluded: full RBAC redesign and replacement of existing identity provider integrations.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria: 
- Conditional SSO policies can block or require step-up for sessions for tenants with restricted residency within 5s of login assertion (end-to-end within SSO flow).
- SCIM reconciliation accuracy improves: mean-time-to-detect-provisioning-drift reduced from ~48h to <6h for high-sensitivity tenants.
- Scheduled access review runs produce reviewer packs with direct links to account-level events, last login, and role-change history; reviewers can mark items as remedied, escalated, or accepted.
- Evidence export bundles include a manifest, per-item signed digests, and an export-level signature using customer or Redwood KMS; bundle verification script included.
- Monitoring: new dashboards track enforcement decisions, reconciliation latency, review completion rate, and evidence export success rate (>99% success).

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Enforcement plane sits as a lightweight policy proxy inserted during authentication/authorization (favors latency over complete context). We will use cached residency tags and a small set of conditionals to keep p99 auth latency <120ms additional overhead.
- SCIM reconciliation moves from batch nightly jobs to an incremental, change-stream-driven pipeline using existing event-store topics; trade-off is increased complexity and more operational streams.
- Evidence signing uses Redwood KMS by default; provide optional customer-managed KMS for enterprise customers with dedicated key control. Using customer KMS adds integration and key rotation complexity.
- Reviewer packs are generated with a time-bounded snapshot to ensure reviewers see consistent data; this increases storage for snapshots but improves audit reproducibility.

Implementation plan (milestones): 
1) Policy model and residency tagging hooks (engineering spike, 1 week) - define policy DSL and residency tag schema.
2) SCIM incremental reconciliation MVP (2 weeks) - wire change-stream, detect drift, surface reasons.
3) SSO conditional enforcement hook (2 weeks) - integrate with SAML/OIDC pipeline, tests for step-up flows.
4) Review automation service + reviewer pack generator (2 weeks) - scheduling, reviewer assignment, minimal Console UI.
5) Evidence bundle format, KMS signing, and export connector (2 weeks) - include verification tooling.
6) End-to-end integration tests, runbook, and docs (1 week).

Rollout plan: start with internal Redwood tenants and three pilot customers (one AI-native startup, one mid-market, one enterprise with residency requirements). Use feature flags and per-tenant toggles. Do a 2-week pilot, collect metrics, iterate.

Monitoring & Alerting: dashboards for enforcement latency, reconciliation lag, review completion rate, export failures. Alerts: reconciliation lag > 6h for any high-sensitivity tenant, evidence export failure rate >1% over 1h window, enforcement error rate spikes.

Security & Compliance: KMS integration must pass security review; export bundles include audit chains. Threat model considers replay of evidence bundles and signing key compromise; mitigations include nonce timestamps, signature verification, and optional customer-managed KMS.

Docs & runbooks: Confluence design doc and runbook links in attachments. PRs will reference this ticket.

Open questions: 
- Should per-tenant residency tagging be editable by customer admins or only set via onboarding flows? (PM leaning: onboarding-only for integrity).
- What retention window do reviewers need for historical snapshots (90 / 180 / 365 days)?
- Customer KMS onboarding UX for non-technical customers.

Risks: 
- Latency regressions during auth flows if policy proxy is mis-optimized.
- Complex SCIM edge-cases causing false positives in drift detection.
- Legal requirements for evidence storage differ by customer jurisdiction.
